injuryReports.name: Zachary Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter was designated for return from injured reserve 16 days ago, so Arizona will need to make a decision on him next week. Carter has yet to play in a game this season after being injured back in August.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: Gaines will miss his sixth straight game in Week 12 due to an ankle injury. With Gaines being on the sidelines again, 2025 sixth-rounder Hayden Conner will project as the Cardinals' top option off the bench on the interior of the offensive line Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Hunter Long
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end returned from injured reserve two weeks ago and has two grabs for 18 yards on three targets in two games since suffering a knee injury. Long is now dealing with an ankle issue. Teagan Quitoriano would see an uptick in snaps behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins if Long is unable to play.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jeremiyah Love
injuryReports.returnComment: Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Josh Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson, who completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in a 34-7 loss to Kansas City in Week 11, thus is set to make his second straight start for the Cardinals. With no teams on bye this week, Johnson's Week 12 fantasy utility is limited to Superflex formats and to fantasy managers scrambling for a short-term injury replacement at the QB position.
injuryReports.injury: Coach Mike LaFleur has ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Sunday's game against the Commanders, which sets the stage for Johnson to start the contest, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Karson Sharar
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Kedon Slovis
injuryReports.returnComment: Slovis had been waived by the Ravens earlier in the week, and while the team hoped to bring him back, the equally quarterback-embattled Cardinals swooped in and claimed him. With that, Slovis returns to the team he played for in 2025.
injuryReports.injury: Slovis was claimed off waivers by the Cardinals on Wednesday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Jack Gibbens
injuryReports.returnComment: Gibbens was able to lead the team in takedowns in Week 11, recording double-digit tackles for the second time in four weeks. The linebacker has now compiled 76 total tackles (33 solo), including 0.5 sacks, while also notching a pass defensed over 11 contests so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Gibbens registered 10 total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Budda Baker
injuryReports.returnComment: Baker was able to register at least six stops for the fourth week in a row and seventh time overall this year. The safety is about as steady as they come, compiling 74 total tackles (36 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Baker recorded six total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Mack Wilson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson was able to register at least eight stops for the second straight week and fifth time overall this season. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (35 solo), two passes defensed and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson recorded eight total tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after drawing three targets in Week 10, as both Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace were clearly ahead of him Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay logged 81 kickoff-return yards in the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season and therefore doesn't possess any fantasy relevance at the moment.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins caught his lone target for four yards during the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko caught one of five targets for a two-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Zay Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.
injuryReports.injury: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Harrison Wallace III
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.

injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing with their third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, the Cardinals have mustered a total of 13 points over their last two games. Ryland has minimal fantasy appeal in an offense struggling to simply move the ball. On the season, he's 22-for-24 on field-goal tries and 17-for-18 on PATs across 11 games.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland made his lone extra-point attempt in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Teagan Quitoriano
injuryReports.returnComment: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.
injuryReports.injury: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.
injuryReports.injury: Knight carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Allgeier
injuryReports.returnComment: Game script fairly quickly put the Cardinals' running game in mothballs, and Allgeier wound up splitting the backfield workload nearly equally with Bam Knight, who picked up 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Allgeier has gone three straight games without reaching 50 rushing yards or getting into the end zone, but those games were also against very tough opponents (the Seahawks in Week 9 and the Rams in Week 10). The fifth-year RB could find a little more running room in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Jeremiyah Love (ankle) might also be ready to rejoin the lineup by then.
injuryReports.injury: Allgeier carried the ball seven times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Trey McBride
injuryReports.returnComment: Working with his fourth quarterback of the season in Josh Johnson, McBride dominated the 40-year-old's attention, as no other Cardinal got more than seven targets or hauled in more than four passes. The star tight end wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, as his longest gain went for a mere nine yards. Carson Beck (back) could be back under center in Week 12 against the Commanders, but that might not improve McBride's outlook, as he saw only five targets in Week 10 during the rookie QB's first NFL start.
injuryReports.injury: McBride caught nine of 14 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. He added four yards on his only carry.

injuryReports.name: Matthew Bergeron
injuryReports.returnComment: Bergeron has started all 10 games this season and played all 631 offensive snaps. It's unclear when he suffered the injury, but Kyle Hinton and Andrew Vorhees are options to replace Bergeron at left guard against Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: DeMarcco Hellams
injuryReports.returnComment: Hellams played a season-high 62 defensive snaps against the Chiefs in Week 10 and logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the loss. He apparently suffered an injury in the contest and will miss his first game of the season. Hellams' main contributions have come on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Billy Bowman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Bowman was unable to participate in practice all week due to a hamstring injury that will sideline the second-year defensive back for the fourth time in the Falcons' last five games. Sydney Brown will operate in an elevated role in the secondary in the absence of Bowman, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Lions on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Kendal Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels has been working through an Achilles injury since October, but his full practice participation Friday was enough for the rookie fourth-rounder to avoid an injury tag for Week 12. He has accumulated 69 tackles (43 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including an interception) and one fumble recovery across 10 games.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Zachariah Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: Branch will join Jahan Dotson (hamstring) on the sidelines in Week 12. Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are Atlanta's available options at wide receiver, while Zaccheaus and Khalil Herbert are the top candidates to handle punt and kickoff returns in Branch's absence. Branch's next opportunity to suit up will be Sunday, Dec. 6, against Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jahan Dotson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dotson hasn't practiced all week, so it wouldn't be surprising if he's ultimately ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings once the Falcons release game designations Friday. Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also remained sidelined at Friday's practice, so Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair may be Atlanta's only healthy and available wide receivers behind Drake London against Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: James Pearce Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Pearce was listed as a limited participant Wednesday but was able to practice without limitations one day later. As such, he should be good to go for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Pearce (back) practiced in full Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Divine Deablo
injuryReports.returnComment: Deablo aggravated a forearm injury against the Bengals in Week 9, which prevented him from playing against the Chiefs in Week 10. He's had additional time to recover courtesy of the bye, and given his absence from Wednesday's injury report, Deablo is on track to play against the Vikings on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Deablo (forearm) was not listed on Wednesday's injury report, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Olamide Zaccheaus
injuryReports.returnComment: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.

injuryReports.name: Jake Moody
injuryReports.returnComment: Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Moody went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Austin Hooper
injuryReports.returnComment: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Drake London
injuryReports.returnComment: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Michael Penix Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Bijan Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Olaivavega Ioane
injuryReports.returnComment: Ioane popped up on Thursday's report as a limited practice participant due to a hand injury. He did not practice Friday, so the rookie first-rounder will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, which leaves Ryan Neuzil and Emery Jones as the top options to start at right guard. Baltimore is on a bye for Week 13, so Ioane's next chance to suit up is Week 14 against Tampa Bay on Sunday, Dec. 13.
injuryReports.injury: Hand

injuryReports.name: Marlon Humphrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Humphrey was benched for Week 11 against the Panthers following derogatory comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. The veteran cornerback will be available Sunday, but his role in the secondary is unclear and may not be known until the Ravens' defense takes the field for the first time. Humphrey has 40 tackles (23 solo), nine pass defenses, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery across 10 games.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters Friday that Humphrey (personal) will be available for Sunday's game against the Texans, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Nnamdi Madubuike
injuryReports.returnComment: Madubuike is set to miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Chargers. With the Ravens on a bye for Week 13, the seventh-year defensive lineman's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13. Broderick Washington and Aeneas Peebles are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Madubuike's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Hawkins' absence will extend to six games due to a knee injury that he sustained in a practice session during Week 7 prep. The Ravens are on a bye for Week 13, so perhaps the extra rest will be enough for Hawkins to be cleared to return for Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Derrick Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Henry has cleared concussion protocol after practicing without limitations Thursday and Friday. He'll try to help the Ravens snap a six-game losing streak Sunday against the Texans. Running room could be hard to come by against a stout Houston front that's allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards per game, though Henry has overcome more than his fair share of daunting matchups over the years.
injuryReports.injury: Henry (concussion) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, per Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio.

injuryReports.name: Mike Green
injuryReports.returnComment: Green's practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a knee injury, but his full session Thursday puts him on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. The second-year edge rusher has accumulated 32 tackles (20 solo), including 7.5 sacks, across 11 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Green (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Rashod Bateman
injuryReports.returnComment: Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Bateman (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Zay Flowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Flowers (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Travis Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones got his first sack of the season in Week 11, and his eight total tackles were a career high. He should retain a big role on the interior of the Ravens' defensive line in a Week 12 tilt at Houston, and he'll be looking to keep up the momentum in that contest.
injuryReports.injury: Jones recorded eight tackles (five solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Trenton Simpson
injuryReports.returnComment: Simpson was able to secure his first double-digit tackle performance of the year, leading the team in takedowns in Week 11. The linebacker has now compiled a career-high 75 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also intercepting a pass and recovering a fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Simpson recorded 10 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamilton was able to notch at least eight takedowns for the second week in a row and fourth time this season. The safety has now registered 78 total tackles (55 solo) and five passes defensed, including an interception, while also forcing a fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Hamilton recorded eight total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Roquan Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith has at least eight tackles in 10 of 11 games this season but has just two games with double-digit tackles. On the season, the veteran linebacker has piled up 91 tackles (40 solo), including 2.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and two forced fumbles on 94 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Smith recorded nine tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cuevas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cuevas continues to draw targets at an impressive clip, tallying three for his second straight game despite only being on the field for 14 of the Ravens' 61 offensive snaps in Week 11. Barring an injury to starter Mark Andrews or rookie fourth-rounder Matt Hibner, though, his role isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats. Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Cuevas caught one of three targets for eight yards during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuryReports.returnComment: Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. He was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Lane didn't garner a target during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Devontez Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: The wide receiver filled a returner role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he could garner more opportunities on special teams following Sunday's success.
injuryReports.injury: Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Riley Patterson
injuryReports.returnComment: Patterson was able to convert his only field-goal try in Week 11, nailing a chip-shot 28-yard attempt in the first quarter. He's now combined to go 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts while making all six of his PATs over two contests as the starting kicker for Baltimore, and he likely will remain in that role for Week 12 with Tyler Loop (groin) sidelined for at least one more contest.
injuryReports.injury: Patterson made his only field-goal attempt and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Matt Hibner
injuryReports.returnComment: Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.
injuryReports.injury: Hibner recorded two catches for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Mark Andrews
injuryReports.returnComment: While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Justice Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Derrick Henry had a strong performance as well but was knocked out of the game in the fourth quarter and got checked for a concussion. Hill was heavily involved in the offense prior to that, however, scoring from 19 yards out in the late in the second quarter. He almost had a second TD earlier in the quarter, but Hill had the ball punched loose at the one-yard line after a 36-yard scamper and saw it bounce out of the end zone for a turnover and a touchback. Henry cleared the concussion protocol after the game and figures to be active in the Week 12 against the Texans, but Hill's usage appears to be on the upswing as the Ravens' No. 2 back.
injuryReports.injury: Hill carried the ball six times for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuryReports.returnComment: It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. He added seven rushing yards on two carries.

injuryReports.name: Feleipe Franks
injuryReports.returnComment: Franks popped up on the Panthers' injury report with a wrist injury Thursday, and now there's a cloud over his status for Week 12. He may end up taking an injury designation into game day if he's not able to upgrade to full participation at practice Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Bobby Okereke
injuryReports.returnComment: Okereke has been sidelined for the Panthers' last three games because of a foot injury, and his availability for Week 12 is now in doubt. Unless he's able to return to practice Saturday, it's not likely he'll be able to suit up Monday against the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Mitchell Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: Evans took a step in the right direction by practicing to some extent Friday after being listed as non-participant on Thursday's estimate. He'll have one more chance to reach full participation Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers. Evans had his best game of 2026 in the Week 11 win over Baltimore, catching all five of his targets for 44 yards and his first touchdown of the season.
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Tommy Tremble
injuryReports.returnComment: Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks has shed any practice limitations, but he'll still need to be added back to the active roster to play Monday in Tampa Bay. Even if Brooks gets the green light to suit up and is activated by the Panthers, he'll likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind Chuba Hubbard against Tampa Bay's excellent run defense.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Darren Waller
injuryReports.returnComment: Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jackson Kuwatch
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Patrick Jones II
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Thomas Incoom
injuryReports.returnComment: Incoom was placed on injured reserve in late October due to a calf injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Eagles. Regardless of his practice participation over the next three days, the Panthers would have to activate Incoom from injured reserve in order for him to be available for Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Tyrel Dodson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dodson came up big for the Panthers in the win, forcing two turnovers, including a game-clinching  interception of Jacoby Brissett late in the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old has now totaled seven or more tackles in three consecutive games and he will look to maintain this level of production during the Week 12 matchup versus the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: Dodson tallied eight tackles (five solo), an interception and a fumble recovery during Carolina's win over the Ravens on Sunday,

injuryReports.name: Brady Christensen
injuryReports.returnComment: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Devin Lloyd
injuryReports.returnComment: The four tackles matched Lloyd's season low in a game this season, which he's done three times in nine contests. While he doesn't post huge tackle numbers, Lloyd makes noise in other areas of the box score. He's piled up 67 tackles (39 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and five pass breakups, including three interceptions, on 94 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Lloyd recorded four tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Legette
injuryReports.returnComment: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: John Metchie III
injuryReports.returnComment: Metchie and Bryce Young connected on a 19-yard pass late in the third quarter to set the Panthers up in the red zone, and the drive ended four plays later on a 33-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Metchie has caught one pass in each of his last two outings, and the fifth-year pro is firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the wide-receiver depth chart. The Panthers will hit the road in Week 12 for a crucial NFC South clash against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Metchie caught one of three targets for 19 yards during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Trevor Etienne
injuryReports.returnComment: Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the modest playing time, the running back made an impact across the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, whose role is as entrenched as any player at his position in the league.
injuryReports.injury: Etienne rushed six times for 29 yards, caught one pass for seven yards, logged 36 kickoff-return yards and recorded eight punt-return yards in the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuryReports.returnComment: Fitzgerald was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the second straight week and seventh time overall this season. The kicker made a 33-yard field goal in the third quarter before he converted a 37-yarder with 1:44 left in the fourth quarter, ultimately putting the Panthers in front 35-33. Fitzgerald now has gone 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts, including 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, while converting 21 of 26 extra-point tries over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Fitzgerald went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Jaycee Horn
injuryReports.returnComment: Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Jalen Coker
injuryReports.returnComment: Coker endured a helmet-to-helmet hit at the end of a six-yard catch in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win against the Ravens, getting shaken up in the process. Afterward, be reportedly entered the concussion protocol, but one day later he doesn't have a head injury. Coker thus is in the clear ahead of next Monday's game at Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Hrad coach Dave Canales said Monday that Coker has been cleared from the concussion protocol, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Young
injuryReports.returnComment: The fourth-year QB posted his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3 percent) while tossing multiple TDs for the third time in the last six contests, a stretch in which he's compiled a 9:5 TD:INT. Both of Young's scores came in the first half, as he connected with Mitchell Evans on a 23-yard TD and Tetairoa McMillan on a seven-yard strike. Young will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-33 win over Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis was a full participant at practice all week, but he's still on injured reserve with his hamstring injury as of Friday. It looks like he might have to wait one more week to return to game action. If so, 2024 fifth-rounder Josh Newton will likely continue to get increased reps at cornerback against a pass-first Saints offense.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Dalton Risner
injuryReports.returnComment: Risner will sit out his second consecutive contest in Week 12 because of a knee injury he sustained back in Week 10 versus the Steelers. In his stead, 2025 fifth-rounder Jalen Rivers figures to make another start at right guard.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas had his 21-day window to return from IR opened Nov. 12, so the Bengals are running out of time to add him back to the active roster before he would need to miss the remainder of the season. If Iosivas isn't activated ahead of Sunday's game, expect such a move to transpire early the following week before the Bengals travel to Cleveland. Dohnte Meyers has been filling in as Cincinnati's No. 3 WR during Iosivas' ongoing absence.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR "the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger has apparently overcome his quadriceps injury after being declared inactive for Monday night's loss to the Commanders. The reserve safety is set to practice in full capacity through Week 12 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Dugger (quadriceps) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jack Endries
injuryReports.returnComment: Endries reeled in a career-high four passes while playing 15 snaps on offense in Week 11. The rookie is still behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample in the pecking order at tight end ahead of Week 12 versus the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Endries caught four of five targets for 33 yards during Monday night's 22-20 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Colbie Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Young reeled in his first pass since Week 3, and he notched his first career touchdown in the process. The wide receiver connected with quarterback Joe Burrow for a four-yard score in the third quarter, momentarily providing Cincinnati with a 17-10 lead. Young's 22 offensive snaps ranked third at his position behind Ja'Marr Chase (56) and Tee Higgins (56) while ahead of Dohnte Meyers (21), but Young may revert to a smaller role on offense with Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on track to return in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Young caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Monday night's 22-20 loss to the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Drew Sample
injuryReports.returnComment: After catching a touchdown pass from Joe Burrow in Week 10 against the Steelers, Sample saw only one target from the superstar quarterback during Monday's loss. Sample has caught one pass or zero in seven of 10 regular-season games and has an 11-72-2 receiving line on 12 targets while operating as the Bengals' TE2 behind Mike Gesicki.
injuryReports.injury: Sample caught his lone target for nine yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: After both teams went scoreless in a rainy first quarter, McPherson put the Bengals on the board with a 38-yard field goal in the second. He nailed a 56-yarder late in the fourth to give the Bengals a 20-19 lead, but his would-be game winner didn't come to pass as the Commanders raced down the field to set up Drew Stevens for a 26-yard field goal to seal the win for Washington. McPherson has made only five field goals (on six attempts) over the Bengals' last five games, but his 35 point-afters are second-most in the NFL behind Eddy Pineiro (36). The Bengals will head back home for Week 12 against the Saints, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in points allowed per game (25.7).
injuryReports.injury: McPherson made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of Meyers' production came on special teams as a returner, and his one catch was his fewest since Week 7 against the Ravens, when he failed to record a reception. He's caught two passes or fewer in seven of 10 regular-season games, and his minimal role on offense would shrink even more once Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is cleared to return from injured reserve. The Bengals will head home for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught one of two passes for two yards, returned six kickoffs for 150 yards and returned one punt for five yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: The Commanders' defense focused its attention toward slowing down both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. That opened up the field for Perine, with most of his production coming on a 44-yard catch late in the second quarter, and the drive ended two plays later with a 31-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Higgins. Perine finished second on the Bengals in both catches and receiving yards behind tight end Mike Gesicki, and the RB's 26 rushing yards were well ahead of Chase Brown's six. Perine has at least 10 touches in each of his last three games, but Cincinnati's offense is mustering only 79.4 rushing yards per game, which is third-worst in the NFL. Given Brown's struggles this season, Perine could take on a larger role in the backfield for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Perine turned six carries into 26 yards and caught all four of his targets for 71 yards during the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end finished with a team-high yardage total while coming just a yard short of equaling his best tally of the season as well. Gesicki's biggest catch came late in the fourth quarter on the Bengals' final drive, when he hauled in a 32-yard pass from Joe Burrow over the middle to get the Bengals down to  the Commanders' 33-yard line. Gesicki's production continues to have some game-to-game volatility, but he'll draw another favorable matchup in a Week 12 home clash with the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki brought in five of six targets for 77 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: As his final line indicates, Brown was completely stonewalled by a talented Commanders run defense, although backfield mate Samaje Perine, who equaled Brown's carry total, was able to average 4.3 yards per tote with his opportunities and  added 71 receiving yards. Brown did find a way to make his usual impact as a receiver, tying for the team lead in receptions and finishing second in targets to Ja'Marr Chase. Brown's carry and rushing yardage totals were both season lows, but he should have appreciably better conditions for production on the ground in a Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Brown rushed six times for six yards and brought in five of eight targets for 30 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: The Commanders focused on keeping Chase in check after his 231-yard outburst against the Steelers in Week 10, and they executed that plan to near perfection. The superstar wideout finished with his third-lowest yardage total of the season, and his sparsest since Week 4. Chase still extended his streak of five-plus-catch efforts to six games, and he'll look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 12 home matchup against a vulnerable Saints defense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Chase secured five of nine targets for 31 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bengals offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Bryan Cook
injuryReports.returnComment: The safety suffered a right ankle injury late in the first half and was questionable to return. Now that he's back, he should be able to resume his role in the lineup at free safety.
injuryReports.injury: Cook (ankle) has returned to Monday night's matchup with the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Brian Parker II
injuryReports.returnComment: Parker had been on IR all season due to a knee injury but was added back to the 53-man roster after turning in five consecutive full practices upon having his 21-day evaluation window opened Nov. 12. He'll serve as a depth option at guard during Monday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: The Bengals reinstated Parker from injured reserve and list him as active for Monday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Swayze Bozeman
injuryReports.returnComment: Bozeman was designated for return from IR on Thursday and needed just three full practices before the Bengals were comfortable adding him back to the 53-man roster. While serving mainly as a special-teams contributor, Bozeman tallied four tackles through the first five weeks of the season before landing on IR due to a broken forearm.
injuryReports.injury: The Bengals reinstated Bozeman (forearm) from injured reserve and list him as active  for Monday's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Dax Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill was absent from practice for the entire week due to an illness, but he is now good to go for Monday Night Football. The 26-year-old will operate in his starting role at slot cornerback versus Washington.
injuryReports.injury: Hill (illness) is active for Monday night's contest against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Oren Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Joe Flacco
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.
injuryReports.injury: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.

injuryReports.name: Austin Barber
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-rounder didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee injury, but he drew the questionable tag after ending Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Zak Zinter would likely start at right guard in the event that Barber is not cleared to play Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Derek Barnett
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran edge rusher was injured in Week 10 against the Texans but was able to return to the contest. The Week 11 bye wasn't enough time for Barnett to get right to play against Las Vegas. Sam Williams and Jamree Kromah will see elevated snaps along the defensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Isaiah McGuire
injuryReports.returnComment: After back-to-back DNPs to begin the practice week, McGuire was limited Friday. It was apparently enough to avoid an injury designation altogether for Sunday night. McGuire has started all 10 games this season, producing 27 tackles (13 solo), including 4.0 sacks, on a career-high 63 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: McGuire (calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Ronnie Hickman
injuryReports.returnComment: Hickman missed the Browns' last game before their Week 11 bye, but he's apparently cleared concussion protocol since and will be available in Week 12. He figures to start at safety next to Grant Delpit on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Hickman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Quincy Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The linebacker was limited Wednesday and Thursday before logging a full practice Friday. Williams has started all 10 games this season, producing 71 tackles (42 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups and four forced fumbles across 95 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Williams (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Raheim Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Denzel Boston
injuryReports.returnComment: With Boston now on track to log a trio of 'DNP' listings this week, his status for Sunday night's game against the Raiders is cloudy. Friday's final injury report will reveal whether the Browns' starting WR has any chance to play versus Las Vegas or is ruled out ahead of Week 12 action.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Blake Whiteheart
injuryReports.returnComment: Whiteheart popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a hip issue but should be good to go for Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has caught four of his seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Whiteheart was listed as full participant in Cleveland's practice estimate Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Browns didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but the fact that Fannin was estimated as a full participant Thursday indicates that the second-year tight end is on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Fannin has caught at least six passes in three of his last four outings, and has compiled a 25-378-1 receiving line on 32 targets over that span.
injuryReports.injury: Fannin (groin) was listed as a full practice participant on Thursday's injury report, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyson Campbell
injuryReports.returnComment: Campbell's three defended passes matched his season total heading into the contest. The cornerback's biggest moment of the day was intercepting C.J. Stroud at the Cleveland 24-yard line with 48 seconds left in the first half. Campbell's turnover likely stole at least three points from the Texans in a game that was decided by the same swing.
injuryReports.injury: Campbell logged five tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including one interception, in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Carson Schwesinger
injuryReports.returnComment: Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.
injuryReports.injury: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (eight solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Corley
injuryReports.returnComment: Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.
injuryReports.injury: Corley caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in addition to returning two kicks for 51 yards during Cleveland's win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tylan Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Texans. He also recorded one tackle in kick coverage.

injuryReports.name: Andre Szmyt
injuryReports.returnComment: Szmyt knocked through field goals from 49 and 26 yards in Sunday's contest. The kicker stumbled in the fourth quarter, missing a 54-yard attempt with 11:02 remaining that would've brought the game within a point. Szmyt is now 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 15-for-16 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Szmyt made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three of his PATs in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
injuryReports.returnComment: Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.
injuryReports.injury: McLaughlin was limited to one snap on offense and none on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Sampson
injuryReports.returnComment: Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.
injuryReports.injury: Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Jerry Jeudy
injuryReports.returnComment: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.
injuryReports.injury: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: KC Concepcion
injuryReports.returnComment: Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.
injuryReports.injury: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry.

injuryReports.name: Deshaun Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Wyatt Teller
injuryReports.returnComment: Teller didn't play against the Colts in Week 11 due to a back injury, but he's been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's contest. He could start at left guard for the Texans in the absence of Keylan Rutledge (neck).
injuryReports.injury: Teller (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Keylan Rutledge
injuryReports.returnComment: Rutledge was not cleared to practice due to a neck injury that he sustained in the Texans' Week 11 win over the Colts. He won't be available Sunday, so Febechi Nwaiwu will likely draw the start at left guard. Rutledge's next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Steelers on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Danielle Hunter
injuryReports.returnComment: Hunter is set to miss a third consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. In his absence, Jadeveon Clowney and Dominique Robinson will continue to operate in elevated roles on the Texans' defensive front opposite NFL sack leader Will Anderson. Hunter's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Steelers on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Brevin Jordan
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end logged a trio of DNPs this week and will miss a third straight contest. With Jordan remaining sidelined, Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover will be the healthy options at the position for Houston. Jordan has two catches for 12 yards on two targets across five contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: Finger

injuryReports.name: Sheldon Rankins
injuryReports.returnComment: Rankins missed Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 11 against the Colts. He logged a limited session Thursday, and Friday's full practice was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. The veteran defensive tackle has accumulated 25 tackles (17 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Rankins (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: David Montgomery
injuryReports.returnComment: Marks was in the league's concussion protocol for Week 11, when Montgomery led the Texans backfield with 26 carries for 107 yards and three catches (on four targets) for 17 yards in a 26-3 win over the Colts. Marks' return means the second-year pro and Montgomery will share the field Sunday for the first time since Week 5 against the Titans, when the latter suffered a groin injury that caused him to miss the Texans' next four games. The duo should split work Sunday against a Baltimore defense that has given up at least 146 rushing yards in three of the team's last four games (all losses).
injuryReports.injury: Montgomery operated as the Texans' RB1 against the Colts in Week 11, but he could see a dip in touches due to the impending return of Woody Marks (concussion) for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Schultz
injuryReports.returnComment: Schultz practiced without limitations Friday, shedding any doubts about his availability after an illness limited his participation Thursday. The Ravens have allowed seven TDs to TEs this season, which is seventh most in the NFL, but Schultz has scored only once all season and is coming off consecutive one-catch performances.
injuryReports.injury: Schultz (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Kayshon Boutte
injuryReports.returnComment: Boutte's absence will coincide with the return of Marvin Harrison (hamstring) from a two-game absence. Harrison will join Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson while Boutte sits out due to an hip injury the latter sustained in last Thursday's win over the Colts, which subsequently prevented Boutte from practicing in any capacity during Week 12 prep. Boutte's next chance to take the field will be Sunday, Dec. 6, at Pittsburgh.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Woody Marks
injuryReports.returnComment: Marks, who was inactive Nov. 19 against the Colts, logged 'full' listings at practice Wednesday through Friday and now has gained clearance to rejoin the lineup after being sidelined for one game. His Week 11 absence coincided with the return to action of fellow RB David Montgomery, and now that both backs are available for the first time since Week 5, look for Marks to see a noticeable dip in volume while sharing touches with Montgomery, who logged 26 carries versus Indianapolis.
injuryReports.injury: Marks (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Jake Hummel
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Abdomen

injuryReports.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Harrison has missed the Texans' last two contests, but after a limited practice Wednesday, the wideout's full participation Thursday sets the stage for him to return to action Sunday against the Ravens. Given Harrison's modest production over three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, he profiles as a speculative fantasy lineup option in Week 12, with Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip, 'DNP' Thursday) also in Houston's WR mix.
injuryReports.injury: Harrison (hamstring) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: M.J. Stewart
injuryReports.returnComment: With the return of Reed Blankenship to the starting lineup, Stewart was relegated to special teams. The strong safety played 17 snaps but did not appear in the box score.
injuryReports.injury: Stewart played 17 special-teams snaps in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Henry To'oTo'o
injuryReports.returnComment: To'oTo'o played 100 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps for the second straight week. The linebacker was on the field for all 48 plays, logging four solo tackles in the effort.
injuryReports.injury: To'oTo'o accumulated six tackles (four solo) in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Will Anderson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson extended his NFL sacks lead to 11.5 in Thursday's contest. The pass rusher is amassing another strong season to contend for Defensive Player of the Year. Anderson finished 2025 with 12.0 sacks and is set to surpass that personal record this season.
injuryReports.injury: Anderson logged five tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Foster Moreau
injuryReports.returnComment: Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those contests. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal unless Schultz were to miss time.
injuryReports.injury: Moreau brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
injuryReports.returnComment: Fairbairn's only field goal of the night was a 27-yarder with 15 seconds remaining in the first half. The kicker is 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PATs over 10 regular-season games so far in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Fairbairn made his sole field-goal attempt and all three PATs in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Emari Demercado
injuryReports.returnComment: With Woody Marks (concussion) inactive, Demercado played the complementary role behind lead back David Montgomery, who rushed 26 times for 107 yards in his return from a multi-week groin injury. Demercado was picked up off waivers from Dallas last month.
injuryReports.injury: Demercado rushed five times for 33 yards and caught both of his targets for minus-four yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Hutchinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.
injuryReports.injury: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Marlin Klein
injuryReports.returnComment: Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tank Dell
injuryReports.returnComment: The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: C.J. Stroud
injuryReports.returnComment: Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nico Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jerry Tillery
injuryReports.returnComment: Tillery will miss a third consecutive game due to a calf injury, so Tim Smith and Kevin Givens will both continue to operate in slightly elevated roles on the interior defensive line behind Grover Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore. The Colts are on a bye for Week 13, so Tillery's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Jalen Travis
injuryReports.returnComment: Travis will miss a third straight game, so Matt Goncalves should make another start at right tackle for the Colts.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Bernhard Raimann
injuryReports.returnComment: Raimann was injured in the Colts' Week 10 win over the Dolphins and missed the team's Week 11 loss to the Texans. He's started 10 games at left tackle this season.
injuryReports.injury: Raimann (concussion) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports.

injuryReports.name: Cam Taylor-Britt
injuryReports.returnComment: The cornerback was designated for return from injured reserve earlier in the week and was a full participant all three practice days. Taylor-Britt appears to have a good chance at being activated and playing Sunday. He hasn't played since Week 7 against the Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Drew Ogletree
injuryReports.returnComment: Ogletree sat out practice Friday after logging a full session Thursday, casting doubt back onto his availability for Week 12. If he can't play Sunday, it would likely mean increased snaps at tight end for veteran Pharaoh Brown.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Will Mallory
injuryReports.returnComment: Mallory is set to miss a fourth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. The Colts are on bye for Week 13, so his next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Drew Ogletree (knee) is listed as questionable after stringing together a DNP-FP-DNP practice log, and if he cannot play Sunday, then Pharaoh Brown would serve as the Colts' TE2 behind Tyler Warren.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Charvarius Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: Ward failed to practice in any capacity during Week 12 prep, and the veteran defensive back will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a knee injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Dolphins. He'll have additional time to rest thanks to the Week 13 bye, and Ward will aim to return for Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Johnathan Edwards, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris are all candidates to start opposite Sauce Gardner at outside cornerback for Sunday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Seth McGowan
injuryReports.returnComment: DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Caden Curry
injuryReports.returnComment: Curry was placed on the Colts' injured reserve Tuesday, and head coach Shane Steichen informed reporters Wednesday that the rookie sixth-rounder's wrist injury was severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery. Curry will end his first NFL campaign with 26 tackles (14 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two fumble recoveries across 11 regular-season games. His absence means Carl Lawson, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and George Gumbs are all in line for more rotational snaps at defensive end.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist
