injuryReports.name: Sauce Gardner
injuryReports.returnComment: Gardner did not play in the Colts' Week 11 loss to the Texans due to a calf injury. The cornerback has recovered since Thursday's contest and is all set to practice in full throughout Week 12 prep. Gardner's fellow starting cornerback Charvarius Ward (knee) also missed Week 11 and was a limited participant Wednesday, meaning the Colts could get both corners back for Sunday against the Giants.
injuryReports.injury: Gardner (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Alec Pierce
injuryReports.returnComment: Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.
injuryReports.injury: Heel

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Taylor is slated to take his first extended snaps alongside Richardson since the 2024 season, when the two started together 10 times. The threat that Richardson presented to defenses as a runner seemed to aid Taylor's own effectiveness, as the running back averaged 4.8 yards per carry and scored eight touchdowns over that 10-game stretch. Now two years later, the Colts have a much less formidable offensive line in place and few established pass-catching weapons that defenses need to hone in on, so Taylor will likely be hard-pressed to match the lofty production he previously achieved with Richardson under center. Additionally, the 3-8 Colts may be cognizant of not overworking Taylor amid a losing season, though the loss of top backup Seth McGowan (hamstring) for at least Week 12 may result in Taylor seeing a slight uptick in opportunities after he played fewer than 70 percent of snaps in each of the last five games and averaged 16.6 touches in those contests.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor will be joined in the backfield in Sunday's game against the Giants by Anthony Richardson, who was named the Colts' new starting quarterback after Daniel Jones was cut Friday, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports.

injuryReports.name: Carl Lawson
injuryReports.returnComment: In a corresponding transaction, the Colts placed rookie sixth-round defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. In his one appearance so far this season back in Week 8 at Jacksonville, Lawson played just eight defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Indianapolis signed Lawson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Shane Buechele
injuryReports.returnComment: Buechele takes the QB No. 3 spot in Indy behind Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. The 28-year-old spent the previous 11 weeks of the NFL season with Buffalo, splitting time on the active roster and practice squad.
injuryReports.injury: The Colts signed Buechele off the Bills' practice squad Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: DJ Giddens
injuryReports.returnComment: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that McGowan "will miss some time" but didn't specify how long the absence may be. For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.
injuryReports.injury: Giddens will likely move up to the No. 2 RB role for the Colts in the short term, as Seth McGowan is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Pharaoh Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: For the second week in a row, Brown ended up seeing more snaps on special teams (11) than offense. Through four games with Indianapolis, Brown has drawn just one target, which he turned into a seven-yard reception during a Week 6 loss to the Titans.
injuryReports.injury: Brown went without a target while playing eight of the Colts' 50 offensive snaps in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Boettcher
injuryReports.returnComment: Boettcher finished Thursday's game tied for the fourth-most tackles on the Colts. The rookie fourth-rounder has started in each of Indianapolis' last three games, which has lined up with the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR). Boettcher is up to 50 tackles (16 solo) through 11 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Boettcher recorded six tackles (three solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Adetomiwa Adebawore
injuryReports.returnComment: Adebawore recorded his fifth sack of the season early in the third quarter, when he took down C.J. Stroud for a seven-yard loss. Adebawore has already set a career-high in sacks through 11 regular-season games and has accumulated 31 tackles (15 solo), one defense and a scoop-and-score in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Adebawore finished Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans with seven tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks.

injuryReports.name: A.J. Haulcy
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-rounder recorded the first interception of his career in the first quarter, when a pass from C.J. Stroud intended for Nico Collins bounced off Haulcy's helmet, off the hands of Cam Bynum and into Haulcy's arms. The LSU product is up to 53 tackles (30 solo) and three pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Haulcy logged nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: CJ Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a busy night for the rookie second-rounder, who finished with a career-high in stops while logging double-digit tackles for the third time this season. Allen has 45 total tackles over his last four outings, and most of that extra playing time has come in the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR).
injuryReports.injury: Allen posted 16 tackles (seven solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Quez Watkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.
injuryReports.injury: Watkins caught one of his three targets for 26 yards during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Dulin
injuryReports.returnComment: Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Dulin caught two of his four targets for 30 yards and assisted on two tackles on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Deion Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.
injuryReports.injury: Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Spencer Shrader
injuryReports.returnComment: Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after the Colts waived Daniel Jones on Friday, which paves the way for Anthony Richardson to start under center in Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Walker Little
injuryReports.returnComment: Little injured his knee in Week 11 against the Giants. However, he's been cleared to play Sunday after stringing together three consecutive limited practices and will start at left tackle against Tennessee.
injuryReports.injury: Little (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Robert Hainsey
injuryReports.returnComment: The Jaguars' center logged three limited practices this week but could miss a second straight contest after he was initially injured in the Week 10 win over Tennessee. Jonah Monheim started at center last Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Matt Dickerson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dickerson did not play against the Giants in Week 11 due to a neck injury, but the UCLA product has been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's AFC South game. The UCLA product has 11 tackles (five solo) and one pass defense across nine games while operating in a rotational role on the Jaguars' interior defensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Dickerson (neck) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Patrick Mekari
injuryReports.returnComment: Mekari got in three limited practices this week but will sit out after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week. He's yet to play this season but appears to be knocking on the door of his season debut. Ezra Cleveland has been manning right guard for Jacksonville.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: B.J. Green II
injuryReports.returnComment: Green has been a full practice participant since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to return, but with his 21-day window set to close, he would need to be activated from IR during Week 13 prep, otherwise he would be sidelined for the rest of the season. His next opportunity to play is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Forearm

injuryReports.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Tuten was held out of practice all week due to a left ankle/foot injury that he aggravated during the Jaguars' Week 11 loss to the Giants. That means Rodriguez will take on the RB1 role for Sunday's game against a Titans defense that has given up at least 40 points in three consecutive games and ranks 25th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (127.1). Rodriguez has logged 63 carries for 261 yards (4.1 YPC) and four touchdowns and caught five of six targets for 49 yards across 10 regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: With Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) ruled out, Rodriguez is slated to operate as the Jaguars' top backfield option for Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Thomas has had a disappointing third season in Jacksonville, mustering a meager 84 receiving yards over his last eight appearances while seemingly having fallen out of favor in coach Liam Coen's offense. Washington's absence against Tennessee's struggling secondary could provide Thomas with an opportunity to turn back the clock and put up a performance reminiscent of the 2024 first-round pick's elite rookie season. Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron also are in line for expanded roles in Jacksonville's wide-receiver room.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas could handle a larger role Sunday against the Titans, as Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports that Parker Washington (shoulder) won't suit up.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cameron
injuryReports.returnComment: Cameron and Brian Thomas are the top candidates to absorb extra targets alongside Jakobi Meyers in Washington's absence. Washington is considered week-to-week, so his absence could extend beyond Week 12. Cameron has 111 receiving yards and a touchdown over the past two games, so the rookie sixth-round pick was trending up even prior to Washington's injury. An increased role against a Titans defense that's giving up the most catches and yards per game to wide receivers could set Cameron up for a breakout performance.
injuryReports.injury: Cameron is in line to handle a larger role Sunday against the Titans, as Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports that Parker Washington (shoulder) won't suit up.

injuryReports.name: Jakobi Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers has managed to shake off an ankle injury that limited his practice participation earlier in the week. He racked up a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 11 loss to the Giants, and Meyers is likely to get plenty of attention from Trevor Lawrence against Tennessee's league-worst secondary Sunday in the absence of top Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (shoulder), giving Meyers appealing upside in nearly all fantasy formats.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.

injuryReports.name: Bhayshul Tuten
injuryReports.returnComment: If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday will factor into his potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so he appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Travis Hunter
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington's shoulder injury seems to have taken a sudden turn for the worse, but the Jaguars had been preparing for their top receiver to be available, so they hadn't been utilizing Hunter much on offense in practice. Hunter should hold down his usual outside cornerback role on defense, but it's likely that most of the targets vacated by Washington will go to some combination of Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and CJ Williams rather than Hunter among Jacksonville's wide receivers.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Liam Coen said Friday that it will be tough to pivot to an increased role for Hunter at wide receiver on short notice after Parker Washington (shoulder) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.

injuryReports.name: Parker Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Danny Striggow
injuryReports.returnComment: Striggow will be good to go for Sunday's matchup against the Titans after clearing the league's concussion protocol. The 24-year-old has compiled 13 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, across nine games this season while playing on both defense and special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Striggow (concussion) was listed as a full participant during Jacksonville's practice estimate Thursday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

injuryReports.name: Jarrian Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones suffered a chest injury during the first half of the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants in Week 12 and did not return. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that Jones' injury isn't a severe one and puts him on track to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Titans. Jones has 26 tackles (19 solo) and eight pass defenses (including an interception) across 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (chest) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Foyesade Oluokun
injuryReports.returnComment: Oluokun had a solid outing despite the loss, logging a team-high nine tackles while playing every defensive snap. The 2018 sixth-round pick has now totaled 77 tackles (48 solo), including 2.0 sacks, two interceptions and a forced fumble across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Oluokun compiled nine tackles (seven solo) during Jacksonville's loss to the Giants on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: LeQuint Allen Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen played 14 offensive snaps behind Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez, and Tuten ended up aggravating his ankle issue in the defeat. If Tuten needs to miss time, Allen could see elevated snaps behind Rodriguez, though Ameer Abdullah also is an option for the Jaguars out of the backfield. Ultimately, Allen is much likelier than not to remain irrelevant in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Allen caught one pass for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Quintin Morris
injuryReports.returnComment: For the first time since Week 3, Morris earned more playing time on offense than rookie Tanner Koziol (four snaps), who had previously been serving as the Jaguars' No. 3 tight end. Koziol offers more of a pass-catching threat at the position, but Morris is the superior blocker and also has a more integral role on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Morris went without a target while logging 11 of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Tanner Koziol
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie fifth-round pick saw his streak of three straight games with a reception come to an end and also had his snap count decline for the fourth week in a row. Koziol ranked fourth in playing time among Jacksonville tight ends, marking the first time since Week 3 that he had played behind Quintin Morris (11 snaps Sunday).
injuryReports.injury: Koziol went without a target while playing four of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Nate Boerkircher
injuryReports.returnComment: Though quarterback Trevor Lawrence dropped back a season-high 50 times on the day and targeted nine different players, Boerkircher wasn't able to earn a look in the passing game. The second-round rookie out of Texas A&M is regarded mainly as a run-blocking specialist, but he had carved out a minor role in the passing attack with at least one reception in each of Jacksonville's previous six contests.
injuryReports.injury: Boerkircher didn't draw a target while playing 22 of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Tim Keenan III
injuryReports.returnComment: Keenan was unable to practice during Week 12 prep due to a knee injury he sustained against the Broncos in Week 11, and his next chance to play is Week 14 against the Chargers on Sunday, Dec. 13. The Raiders will enter the weekend with only two healthy defensive lineman on the 53-man roster in Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jackson Powers-Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Powers-Johnson was injured in Friday's practice, and coach Klint Kubiak suggested it could be a serious injury, according to Sam Warren of The Athletic. He hasn't logged an offensive snap since Week 5 after opening the season as the Raiders' starting right guard. Trey Zuhn has been manning the position.
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Adam Butler
injuryReports.returnComment: The defensive lineman sustained a concussion last Sunday against the Broncos and will miss at least one contest while he works through the protocol. With Tim Keenan (knee) also out against Cleveland and JJ Pegues (elbow) questionable, the Raiders may be especially thin up front Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Tonka Hemingway
injuryReports.returnComment: Hemingway missed the final two practices of Week 12 prep due to what was classified as a stinger, and the second-year defensive tackle will end up missing his second consecutive game. He'll join Adam Butler (concussion) and Tim Keenan (knee) on the sidelines Sunday, and that leaves Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi as the only healthy defensive lineman on the Raiders' active roster heading into the weekend. With the Raiders on a bye for Week 13, Hemingway's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Chargers on Sunday, Dec. 13.
injuryReports.injury: Upper Body

injuryReports.name: Darrell Luter Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: JJ Pegues
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Brock Bowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Sam Warren of The Athletic, Bowers didn't practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. It's unclear if the star TE's 'DNP' to close the week was maintenance or setback related, but the Raiders' late kickoff presents an issue for those considering Bowers in Week 12 fantasy lineups. As one of the marquee names carrying a 'questionable' tag into the weekend, look for added context regarding his status to arrive no later than Saturday night or Sunday morning via the usual notable NFL insiders.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Patrick Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in late October due to a neck injury. His ability to practice in full is an encouraging sign, but Johnson would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Dareke Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Young was diagnosed with a stinger in the first half of the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos and did not return. However, his ability to practice in full Wednesday indicates that the fifth-year wide receiver will be available for Sunday's road game against the Browns. Young has mostly operated on special teams this season and has not been targeted in the passing game since Week 4 against the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Young (stinger) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Chinn
injuryReports.returnComment: Chinn was on the field for all 73 of the team's defensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to notch at least seven stops for the seventh straight game. The safety has now registered 79 total tackles (52 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over 11 contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: Chinn recorded seven total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Quay Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was Walker's fourth game this season with double-digit tackles, and he's now up to 91 tackles (39 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pair of fumble recoveries across 11 games this season. He's taken a bit of a back seat to Nakobe Dean in the tackles department for Las Vegas, as Dean leads the NFL with his 119 total tackles.
injuryReports.injury: Walker recorded 11 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Nakobe Dean
injuryReports.returnComment: The linebacker has at least a dozen tackles in seven of 10 games this season and leads the NFL with 119 tackles (56 solo). He's also recorded three pass breakups, including one interception, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery while playing 100 percent of the Raiders' defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Dean recorded 12 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Ian Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: Thomas had the opportunity to step into the TE2 role behind Michael Mayer on Sunday due to the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps). Thomas' 35 offensive snaps were his most of the season, and he made his lone target from Fernando Mendoza count, with the duo connecting on a 19-yard touchdown pass late in the third quarter to tie the game up at 17-17. Thomas has seven catches on as many targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns through 11 regular-season games, although he would revert to being the No. 3 tight end in Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29 if Bowers is cleared to return for that contest.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown during the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Matt Gay
injuryReports.returnComment: Gay has attempted only one field goal in three of his last four outings, and his lone try Sunday was a chip shot from 28 yards out. He's 22-for-24 on field-goal attempts through 11 regular-season games, and he's ranked fifth in the NFL in made field goals. The Raiders will hit the road for Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Gay made his lone field-goal attempt and all three of his extra-point tries during the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Nailor
injuryReports.returnComment: Nailor caught one pass for the second straight week, and he has exceeded 20 receiving yards only one time since Week 1. The wide receiver was unable to capitalize on the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle) in Week 11, and Nailor figures to remain an unattractive fantasy option in Week 12 against the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Nailor caught one of five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Tre Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: Tucker finished with a team-high 10 targets, but he was unable to get on the same page with quarterback Fernando Mendoza for the majority of the game. Most of the wide receiver's production came on a 39-yard catch in the fourth quarter, and he has now combined to reel in three of 12 targets for 59 yards over Mendoza's first two career starts.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker caught two of 10 targets for 50 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Mike Washington Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: With only seven targets and four catches through 11 games to begin his career, Washington requires volume on the ground to produce, which is difficult to come by in a backfield led by Ashton Jeanty. And Jeanty was the engine of the Raiders offense Sunday, racking up 16 touches for 169 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD. A rookie fourth-rounder, Washington is averaging just 3.9 yards per carry and has scored only one touchdown ahead of next Sunday's road matchup with the Browns.
injuryReports.injury: Washington turned nine carries into 42 yards during Sunday's 38-24 defeat in Denver.

injuryReports.name: Michael Mayer
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayer missed out on a prime opportunity with top TE Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) inactive in Week 11. When Bowers was out in Weeks 1 and 2 as he recovered from a meniscus trim in his left knee, Mayer went for a combined 9-55-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, but the latter also missed a stretch in the fourth quarter this Sunday due to a back injury. Bowers' status will be worth monitoring this week, as an absence from him next Sunday in Cleveland will set up Mayer for another key chance to produce.
injuryReports.injury: Mayer posted one catch (on four targets) for four yards during Sunday's 38-24 defeat at Denver.

injuryReports.name: Fernando Mendoza
injuryReports.returnComment: After throwing for no touchdowns or interceptions in his first NFL start last Sunday against the Seahawks, Mendoza recorded the first scoring strike of his career on a 68-yard catch and run via RB Ashton Jeanty in Week 11. Mendoza also hooked up with Ian Thomas (19 yards) and Jack Bech (seven yards) for his other two TDs, but he followed up a 58.6 completion percentage in Week 10 with more misfires (19) than connections (18) this Sunday. Mendoza's next chance for game action is next Sunday at Cleveland.
injuryReports.injury: Mendoza was 18-for-37 passing for 267 yards, three touchdowns and one interception and had four carries for 22 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss in Denver.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Jeanty
injuryReports.returnComment: Jeanty's 169 yards from scrimmage amounted to the second-highest single-game total of his career after going for 188 such yards against the Texans in Week 16 of last season. His performance was fueled by a 68-yard catch and run for a touchdown and a 46-yard rush, the latter of which marked his first of 20-plus yards on the campaign. Jeanty also broke a streak of four straight contests falling short of 10 carries, but considering No. 2 RB Mike Washington also earned nine runs in Week 11, the Raiders backfield remains a committee ahead of next Sunday's outing at Cleveland.
injuryReports.injury: Jeanty tallied 11 carries for 79 yards and gathered in five of eight targets for 90 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 loss at Denver.

injuryReports.name: Jack Bech
injuryReports.returnComment: Bech finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tre Tucker (10), and he was able to reel in a seven-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The score was Bech's first since Week 1, and his 88 receiving yards bested his previous season total of 67 yards entering Week 11. The wide receiver appears to have great chemistry with Mendoza, garnering 16 targets over the quarterback's first two career starts.
injuryReports.injury: Bech caught eight of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Kendall Williamson
injuryReports.returnComment: Williamson was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets and logged a pair of limited practices Thursday and Friday following Wednesday's absence. He's yet to play a single defensive snap this season while seeing 129 snaps on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Tuli Tuipulotu
injuryReports.returnComment: An ankle injury prevented Tuipulotu from practicing all week, yet the Chargers have kept the door open for the fourth-year edge rusher to suit up for Sunday's contest. Akheem Mesidor (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which leaves Khalil Mack, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree as the three healthy edge rushers on the Chargers' 53-man roster heading into the weekend.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brenen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: Thompson has not played since Week 2 against the Raiders due to a hamstring injury, and it looks like that trend will continue after the rookie fourth-rounder missed all three practices during Week 12 prep. Assuming he doesn't play Sunday, Thompson's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Tarheeb Still
injuryReports.returnComment: Still did not practice at all during the week after sitting out the Chargers' contest versus the Jets in Week 11 with an ankle injury, but there's apparently still a chance he'll be able to play in Week 12. Otherwise, Isas Waxter might be in line to see an increased snap count at cornerback Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Akheem Mesidor
injuryReports.returnComment: Mesidor was not able to practice at all during the week because of an ankle injury he sustained in Week 11 versus the Jets, and it looks like he might be trending towards missing his first game of the season in Week 12. If he can't go Sunday, it could mean an uptick in reps on the edge for Caleb Murphy.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Daiyan Henley
injuryReports.returnComment: Henley will spend a second straight game on the sidelines due to a knee injury in Week 12. In his absence, veteran Troy Dye could get a start at linebacker next to fellow veteran Del'Shawn Phillips on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: DJ Uiagalelei
injuryReports.returnComment: Uiagalelei got his first taste of NFL regular-season action in Week 11 against the Jets after Herbert suffered a concussion, with the former completing two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown. With Herbert in the league's protocol for head injuries, Uiagalelei will make his first career start Sunday against a New England defense that ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (239.0). Jake Browning also is available to serve as Los Angeles' backup.
injuryReports.injury: Uiagalelei will be the Chargers' starting quarterback against the Patriots on Sunday due to the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Justin Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: At 1-9, the Chargers have zero incentive to rush Herbert back to the field at this stage. His next chance to see game action thus is slated to arrive Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Buccaneers. In Herbet's absence this weekend, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network relays that DJ Uiagalelei is slated to start at QB for the Chargers, with Jake Browning available to back him up.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: David Njoku
injuryReports.returnComment: Njoku was held out of practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. He was cleared to return to practice in a limited capacity Friday, which was enough for the veteran tight end to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will maintain expanded roles on offense in the event that Njoku doesn't play, and Patrick Herbert would be a candidate for elevation from the practice squad to give the Chargers more depth at tight end. That said, the Chargers' offensive potential figures to be limited in Week 12 in the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), with DJ Uiagalelei set to make his first career start.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Keaton Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell tweaked his knee during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 11. The injury prevented the fourth-year pro from practicing all week, and his absence for Sunday's contest means Kimani Vidal should operate in an expanded role in the backfield behind RB1 Omarion Hampton. Mitchell's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Deane Leonard
injuryReports.returnComment: It's not clear when Leonard was injured, as he logged a season-high 70 percent defensive snap share against the Jets last Sunday. Regardless, he's now required to miss at least four games while on IR. Avery Smith and Isas Waxter may get more opportunities in the secondary during Leonard's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Jake Browning
injuryReports.returnComment: Browning joined Los Angeles' practice squad Oct. 13 and had been there since before being promoted to the active roster Thursday. The move could be a bad sign for starting QB Justin Herbert, who is in concussion protocol and could  miss Sunday's clash against New England. Should Herbert miss that game, rookie DJ Uiagalelei would likely log his first NFL start, with Browning working as his backup.
injuryReports.injury: The Chargers signed Browning to their active roster Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Dalvin Tomlinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Tomlinson likely sustained his knee injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The defensive tackle will likely need to return to practice by Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Oronde Gadsden
injuryReports.returnComment: Gadsden ranked third in snaps among Chargers tight ends, finishing only slightly behind Charlie Kolar (30) and David Njoku (25). Despite arguably being the most talented pass catcher of the trio, Gadsden was the only one of the three who failed to draw a target in Week 11. The 2025 fifth-round pick has endured a disappointing sophomore campaign, having thus far put together a 20-179-1 receiving line on 30 targets over 10 games while topping 40 receiving yards on just one occasion.
injuryReports.injury: Gadsden went without a target while taking the field for 23 of the Chargers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Molden
injuryReports.returnComment: The safety has finished with five or more stops in seven of the eight games he's played in this season. Molden has 44 tackles (25 solo), a pass breakup and a fumble recovery in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Molden recorded eight tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Del'Shawn Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: The linebacker recorded at least four stops for the fourth game in a row and the ninth time in 10 games this season. Phillips has 53 tackles (23 solo) and an interception on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Phillips finished with four tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Kolar
injuryReports.returnComment: Kolar was cleared to play Sunday after progressing through the league's concussion protocol, and his 30 offensive snaps were ahead of fellow tight ends David Njoku (25) and Oronde Gadsden (23). Kolar's eight-yard catch midway through the first quarter was the only pass that the fifth-year pro saw from Justin Herbert, but no Chargers pass catcher saw more than five targets other then Ladd McConkey (eight). Kolar has a 16-153-0 line on 24 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Kolar brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Dicker
injuryReports.returnComment: Dicker's field goal was drilled from 52 yards, and he's now 19-for-21 on field-goal tries and 15-for-15 on extra points through 10 games this season. In a Chargers offense struggling mightily to score points, Dicker's fantasy value has tanked this season.
injuryReports.injury: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and all three PATs in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Quentin Johnston
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnston was targeted on just 9.5 percent of Justin Herbert's 21 pass attempts against New York. The wideout has now caught exactly one pass in three straight games and in five of his last six contests. Johnston is a lightly targeted deep threat who will likely continue to see fewer looks if Ladd McConkey is able to maintain his health for an extended period.
injuryReports.injury: Johnston caught one of two targets for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets. He added one yard on one rushing attempt.

injuryReports.name: Kimani Vidal
injuryReports.returnComment: After handling just four touches last week against the Ravens, Vidal saw his usage increase again as he recorded his most scrimmage yards since Week 5. This time, however, his additional volume came at the expense of Keaton Mitchell (knee), who left the game early. Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the Chargers' clear No. 1 RB over the last few contests, but if Mitchell's injury proves to be serious, Vidal could have some deeper-league appeal with the No. 2 role all to himself. He'll look to take advantage of whatever opportunities he gets in Week 12 against the Patriots.
injuryReports.injury: Vidal carried the ball seven times for 36 yards and caught both his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Tre' Harris
injuryReports.returnComment: With Ladd McConkey back in the lineup, Harris' role in the passing attack shrank after he'd turned 12 targets over the prior two games into an 8-92-0 line. Harris' fantasy appeal would collapse even further if Justin Herbert (concussion) ends up missing any time. The second-year wideout will at least get a promising matchup in Week 12 against a vulnerable Patriots secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Harris caught both his targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Ladd McConkey
injuryReports.returnComment: His longest gain went for just 11 yards, but McConkey was deadly in the red zone, connecting with Justin Herbert on scores of 11 and six yards in the fourth quarter as the Chargers tried to mount a late comeback. Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol after the game after taking six sacks, and if he end up missing any time, it would put a big damper on McConkey's fantasy outlook with undrafted rookie DJ Uiagalelei being the Bolts' backup, unless Trey Lance (groin) is able to return from IR. McConkey has had plenty of trouble staying on the field himself this year, of course, and he'll take a 22-323-3 line on 32 targets through seven contests into a Week 12 clash with the Patriots.
injuryReports.injury: McConkey caught five of eight targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Omarion Hampton
injuryReports.returnComment: While he's still not seeing a consistent bell-cow workload, Hampton has turned his season around over the last three games, racking up 254 rushing yards and a TD while averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell left Sunday's game early with a knee injury, but his absence appeared to provide a bigger boost to Kimani Vidal, who wound up logging nine touches and 54 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against the Patriots.
injuryReports.injury: Hampton carried the ball 14 times for 89 yards and caught his only target for four yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Trey Pipkins III
injuryReports.returnComment: Pipkins had been on IR since late September before being activated Saturday. The veteran offensive lineman is now set to give the Chargers' offensive line a boost. Pipkins may work in a rotational role, as Logan Taylor is "locked in" at left guard, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com.
injuryReports.injury: Pipkins (knee) is active for Sunday's matchup against the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Bradley Pinion
injuryReports.returnComment: He'll miss a second straight game, also Jack Browning should get the nod at punter for Miami. He'll likely be busy Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Dante Trader Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Trader was sidelined Week 11 at Buffalo with shoulder and groin injuries, but he's now back to full strength. He projects to start at safety next to rookie fifth-rounder Michael Taaffe against the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Trader (shoulder/groin) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Jets.

injuryReports.name: Jared Wayne
injuryReports.returnComment: Wayne will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6. Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will continue to operate in slightly expanded roles on offense in Wayne's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: JuJu Brents
injuryReports.returnComment: Brents did not participate in any of the three Week 12 practices while recovering from neck and shoulder injuries that he sustained in Week 11 against the Bills. Darrell Baker will likely start opposite Jason Marshall at outside cornerback in the absence of Brents, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Jaylin Simpson
injuryReports.returnComment: Simpson missed the Dolphins' Week 11 loss to the Bills due to a knee injury. The reserve cornerback has since recovered from the issue and is set to log full participation in practices throughout Week 12 prep in anticipation of Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Simpson (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones reports.

injuryReports.name: Zayne Anderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson was thrust into a starting role at safety with Dante Trader (shoulder/groin) inactive, and he made the most of his opportunity. Anderson finished second on the team in tackles while intercepting Bills quarterback Josh Allen in the second quarter and sacking him in the third quarter. If Trader remains sidelined again in Week 12, Anderson will likely get a shot at an encore performance against the Jets on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Anderson recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks, and also intercepted a pass during Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Will Kacmarek
injuryReports.returnComment: After drawing at least one target in each of the previous three games, Kacmarek failed to draw a look from quarterback Kyle McCord, who connected with seven different pass catchers on the day. Kacmarek ran routes on just six of his 21 snaps, as the Dolphins continue to utilize him mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.
injuryReports.injury: Kacmarek went without a target while logging 21 of 57 snaps on offense in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: The eight tackles were actually Brooks' second fewest in a game this season. After leading the NFL with 183 tackles (99 solo) last season and being named a First-Team All-Pro, Brooks has just 92 tackles (40 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass breakups and a forced fumble across 10 starts in 2026. He's still on pace for a sixth straight 100-tackle campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks recorded eight tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Rodriguez
injuryReports.returnComment: With Miami trailing 20-3 in the second quarter, Rodriguez picked off Josh Allen and returned it to Buffalo's 22-yard line to help set up a Dolphins field goal. It was the second-round rookie linebacker's second interception of the season, and his 13 tackles were his third-highest total in a single game. He's up to 93 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two interceptions and a forced fumble while playing 99 percent of the Dolphins' defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Rodriguez recorded 13 tackles (eight solo) and an interception in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: Wright continues to struggle rushing the ball this season, averaging just 1.6 yards per carry across 30 rush attempts. The 23-year-old will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Wright carried the ball five times for 10 yards and returned three kickoffs for 79 yards during Miami's loss to the Bills on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kaytron Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen played 16 special-teams snaps in the contest. The running back did not log an offensive snap, leaving all the rushing work to Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright.
injuryReports.injury: Allen logged 80 kickoff-return yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Chris Bell
injuryReports.returnComment: Bell saw 34 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest but was inefficient with his opportunities. The Dolphins continues to try to involve the third-round rookie, but he's been frequently out of sync with quarterbacks Malik Willis (IR, abdomen) and Kyle McCord.
injuryReports.injury: Bell caught one of his four targets for eight yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kevin Coleman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: With Chris Bell (knee) back from his absence, Coleman reverted to WR4 duties for Miami, playing just 12 of 57 offensive snaps. He has no fantasy appeal while Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington and Bell are healthy. Coleman has been extremely inefficient through 10 games this season, catching just nine of 28 targets for 88 yards and two touchdowns.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Tolbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Tolbert played just eight of the Dolphins' 55 offensive snaps in Week 11, and he drew just one target for the third time in his last five games. Miami will probably continue to lean primarily on Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell at wide receiver in a Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Tolbert caught his only target for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 loss at Buffalo.

injuryReports.name: Daniel Carlson
injuryReports.returnComment: Carlson was signed to the Dolphins' practice squad this past Tuesday, two weeks after being released by the Saints. He served as the Dolphins' kicker Sunday against the Bills, when he made all three of his field-goal attempts in a 27-9 loss for Miami. The Dolphins do not have a kicker on the 53-man roster, so Carlson is almost certain to be elevated for Week 12 against the Jets on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Carlson reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Ronnie Harrison Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Harrison suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. The fact the Dolphins opted to open his practice window after nine weeks suggests Harrison may be nearing a return.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Malik Willis
injuryReports.returnComment: That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.
injuryReports.injury: Abdomen

injuryReports.name: Malik Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: Washington's six targets were third on the team, trailing Caleb Douglas (10) and Greg Dulcich (seven) on a day when Kyle McCord attempted 33 passes. Washington has just one touchdown this season and has yet to reach 70 receiving yards in any game in 2026. There's not much to like about the wideout's fantasy prospects moving forward this season.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught three of six targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills. He rushed two times for 11 yards.

injuryReports.name: Greg Dulcich
injuryReports.returnComment: Dulcich finished second on the team in targets behind wide receiver Caleb Douglas (10), but he failed to exceed 20 receiving yards for the third straight week. The tight end hasn't scored a touchdown this season, and his next chance will come in Week 12 against the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Dulcich caught two of seven targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.

injuryReports.name: Christian Darrisaw
injuryReports.returnComment: The Vikings' left tackle has been playing at less than 100 percent for most of this month and aggravated the issue last Sunday night against the 49ers. Ryan Van Demark replaced Darrisaw at left tackle against San Francisco and figures to draw the Week 12 start.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Harrison Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a thigh injury. In the event that he cannot play Sunday, Theo Jackson would likely start opposite Josh Metellus at safety. Smith has 21 tackles (11 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and five pass defenses (including two interceptions) across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Thigh

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Rodgers
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Emily Leiker of The Minnesota Star Tribune, Rodgers sat out practice again Friday due to his quad injury, and he'll now miss his second straight game in Week 12. In his absence, rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings figures to see an uptick in snaps on the boundary.
injuryReports.injury: Thigh

injuryReports.name: Myles Price
injuryReports.returnComment: Price was limited at practice Wednesday and Thursday but upgraded to full participation Friday and has been cleared to suit up. He, along with Tai Felton and Jauan Jennings, will vie for larger roles alongside Justin Jefferson as the Vikings continue to play without Jordan Addison (thumb) against Atlanta's mediocre secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Price (knee/groin) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Emily Leiker of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.

injuryReports.name: Kyler Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: Murray has been cleared to suit up for the first time since Week 8 after practicing without limitations Friday. He's set to back up Kirk Cousins, who is entrenched as Minnesota's starting QB after being reacquired in a trade with the Raiders.
injuryReports.injury: Murray (hamstring) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Falcons, Emily Leiker of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.

injuryReports.name: Tai Felton
injuryReports.returnComment: Felton stepped up in Addison's absence during the Week 11 loss to San Francisco, leading the Vikings with 12 targets en route to six catches for 42 yards. Jauan Jennings and Myles Price also are candidates for additional targets from Kirk Cousins behind Justin Jefferson against a Falcons defense that gives up the fifth-most passing yards per game.
injuryReports.injury: Felton is poised to maintain an expanded role Sunday against the Falcons, as Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports that Jordan Addison (thumb) will remain sidelined.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Addison
injuryReports.returnComment: Addison thus will miss a third straight contest due to a thumb injury that required surgery. In Addison's continued absence, the Vikings will lean on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver. Addison's next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 6, versus the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Joshua Metellus
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the first time this season that Metellus failed to record a solo tackle, and his 83.3 percent snap count on defense was his lowest of the season, although that was partly due to the Vikings resting their starters in the fourth quarter. Metellus has accumulated 68 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses across 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Metellus posted five assisted tackles during the Vikings' 35-10 loss to the 49ers on Sunday in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Eric Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson had only one tackle Sunday, but it was an impactful one as he took down Brock Purdy for a seven-yard loss in the third quarter to force the 49ers to punt on the next play. In his five outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, Wilson has accumulated 32 tackles (20 solo), including 3.5 sacks.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson recorded 1.0 sacks during the Vikings' 35-10 loss to the 49ers on Sunday in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Ben Yurosek
injuryReports.returnComment: Since being reinstated from injured reserve in Week 5, Yurosek has cleared 40 percent snap shares in five of the Vikings' ensuing six games. However, he remains a fringe part of the passing attack, having thus far mustered a 3-41-0 receiving line on four targets. He ran routes on just nine of his 29 snaps in Week 11, with Yurosek mainly serving as a blocker during his time on the field.
injuryReports.injury: Yurosek failed to draw a target while playing 29 of the Vikings' 67 offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Blake Cashman
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing the Week 10 win over the Packers while dealing with a concussion, Cashman returned from the one-game absence to play 93 percent of the defensive snaps Sunday. He's up to 85 tackles (45 solo), including a career-high 4.5 sacks, seven pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Cashman recorded nine tackles (four solo) in Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Gavin Bartholomew
injuryReports.returnComment: With T.J. Hockenson back in the lineup after being inactive Week 10, Bartholomew played just 18 of 67 offensive snaps as the Vikings' third tight end, also behind Ben Yurosek. Bartholomew has 11 catches for 95 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Bartholomew caught one of three targets for five yards in Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Will Reichard
injuryReports.returnComment: Reichard failed to get the Vikings on the board in the first quarter after his 55-yard field-goal attempt missed to the left. He had the stadium's altitude in his favor when lining up for a 71-yarder on the final play of the first half, but what would have been an NFL record-breaking kick fell just short. Reichard is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts through 10 regular-season games, and each of those misses have come from 50-plus yards. The Vikings will be home in a controlled environment for three of their next four games, starting in Week 12 against the Falcons on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Reichard went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point try during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Mason
injuryReports.returnComment: Mason had one more carry and eight more rushing yards than Aaron Jones, but Jones' totals included an 11-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. They have worked in a near-even split when both veteran RBs have been healthy, but Mason hasn't scored since Week 1. Between his lack of TDs and minimal involvement as a pass catcher (three receptions for six yards in six games), Mason hasn't provided much fantasy value ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.
injuryReports.injury: Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards while catching his lone target for minus-1 yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones tied the game with an 11-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but the 49ers outscored the Vikings 21-3 in the second quarter, forcing Minnesota into a more pass-heavy approach. Jordan Mason led the team with 38 rushing yards on 11 carries. Jones and Mason should continue to split carries in Week 12 against the Falcons, with Jones offering greater upside as a pass catcher.
injuryReports.injury: Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his lone target for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: T.J. Hockenson
injuryReports.returnComment: In his return from a one-game absence, Hockenson finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Justin Jefferson's 86. Hockenson showed promising chemistry with Kirk Cousins after the veteran TE sat out Cousins' return to Minnesota during the Week 10 win over Green Bay. Cousins was under center for the Vikings in the 2023 regular season, when Hockenson set career highs with 95 catches for 960 yards. Hockenson hasn't surpassed 455 yards in a regular season since, though he's on pace to do so this year, with 41 catches for 383 yards and three touchdowns through nine appearances heading into a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.
injuryReports.injury: Hockenson (wrist) caught six of seven targets for 55 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Jauan Jennings
injuryReports.returnComment: Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes, while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.
injuryReports.injury: Jennings caught three of six targets for 20 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Kirk Cousins
injuryReports.returnComment: After throwing a pick-six among his three interceptions when he faced San Francisco's defense in his final game with the Raiders in Week 9, Cousins had another interception returned for a touchdown by the 49ers in the second quarter of Sunday's loss. The Vikings took a 28-10 deficit into the halftime locker room, and Cousins was unable to orchestrate a comeback before Minnesota waved the white flag and inserted Carson Wentz for its final drive. Cousins is still strengthening his grasp on the offense two games into his reunion with the Vikings ahead of a Week 12 visit from the Falcons, with whom Cousins spent the previous two seasons.
injuryReports.injury: Cousins completed 26 of 38 passes for 235 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for no gain.

injuryReports.name: Justin Jefferson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jefferson has experienced an uptick in usage since the Vikings reacquired Kirk Cousins. The star WR has 16 catches for 160 yards on 22 targets in two games with Cousins, though Jefferson hasn't scored since Week 8. Jefferson fumbled at the end of a 25-yard catch in the third quarter, turning what would have been one of his best plays of the night into a lowlight. Another heavy dose of targets from Cousins likely awaits Jefferson in Week 12 against the Falcons.
injuryReports.injury: Jefferson caught seven of nine targets for 86 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Max Brosmer
injuryReports.returnComment: Brosmer will operate as the team's No. 3 option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Kirk Cousins and primary backup Carson Wentz are forced out of the contest.
injuryReports.injury: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but operating as the Vikings' emergency third QB on Sunday night versus the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Jeshaun Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Walter Rouse
injuryReports.returnComment: Rouse missed the Patriots' last game before their bye in Week 11 due to a concussion, but after logging a full practice Friday, it looks like there's a chance he could return in Week 12. If he doesn't, Ben Brown could end up being the Patriots' unquestioned top option off the bench on the interior of the offensive line Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Christian Barmore
injuryReports.returnComment: Barmore first appeared on the Patriots' Week 12 injury report Friday as a DNP, which indicates that the knee issue is a new one for the sixth-year defensive lineman. A late addition to the injury report typically isn't a good sign, but Barmore's official availability may not be known until the Patriots announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff. DaQuan Jones and Joshua Farmer would both be in line for more snaps on defense if Barmore doesn't play.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Robert Spillane
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran linebacker exited the Patriots' Week 10 game against the Lions in Germany with an illness but is fine coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. Across 10 starts this season, Spillane has recorded 58 tackles (25 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two pass breakups and a forced fumble.
injuryReports.injury: Spillane (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Gilliam
injuryReports.returnComment: Gilliam returned from injured reserve in Week 10 against the Lions and is now coming off the bye week, but he's still dealing with the knee issue. The fullback has touched the ball two times on offense this season, logging 71 snaps and another 56 on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Carlton Davis III
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, Davis was unable to participate in any of the Week 12 practices due to a knee injury and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. Charles Woods will likely start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback Sunday in the absence of Davis, whose next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: DeMario Douglas
injuryReports.returnComment: Douglas had 178 yards and a touchdown in a career-best two-game stretch spanning Weeks 8 and 9, but he was limited to one catch for four yards in his most recent appearance, which QB Drake Maye (lower leg) left early. With Tommy DeVito under center in Week 12, Douglas will try to get back on track in New England's banged-up passing game coming out of a bye week.
injuryReports.injury: Douglas is set to maintain a prominent role Sunday against the Chargers, as A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) won't play.

injuryReports.name: Mack Hollins
injuryReports.returnComment: Hollins led the Patriots with five catches for 48 yards in their 35-10 Week 10 loss to the Lions prior to a Week 11 bye. He showed the best chemistry out of New England's pass catchers with Tommy DeVito, who replaced Drake Maye (lower leg) against Detroit and is expected to start Sunday's game. Hollins has 23 catches for 293 yards and one touchdown in six appearances this season.
injuryReports.injury: Hollins is set to work in a starting role Sunday against the Chargers, as A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) won't play.

injuryReports.name: Romeo Doubs
injuryReports.returnComment: Since the Patriots designated Doubs for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged limited listings on injury reports. However, head coach Mike Vrabel told Evan Lazar of the team's official site Friday that Doubs is unlikely to play in Week 12, which now has been confirmed. Doubs will turn his sights to a Week 13 matchup with the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: A.J. Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: With Brown unavailable following the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are in line to handle the team's WR duties in Tommy DeVito's first start of 2026. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs (shoulder) isn't likely to be activated from IR this weekend, so it looks like the earliest either of New England's top two wideouts could be available is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bills.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevenson hurt his knee in Week 9 against Green Bay and initially appeared slated to miss multiple games. However, he surprisingly was able to suit up in Week 10 against Detroit in Munich, Germany, though he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share and gained only five yards on seven touches. Stevenson is now off the injury report entirely to begin Week 12 prep following New England's Week 11 bye, suggesting that the knee issue is no longer a concern. The veteran running back commented Wednesday on his ability to suit up in Week 10, attributing it to "a bunch of recovery" and sharing, "(The trainers) did a good job of just getting me available again... Leg wasn't feeling 100 percent, but I was well enough to go out there and participate with the team and try to help them out a little bit," per Sophie Weller of Patriots Wire. With no practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep, Stevenson should be set to suit up this Sunday  in Los Angeles against the Chargers, when he'll be taking handoffs from QB Tommy DeVito.
injuryReports.injury: Stevenson was not listed on the Patriots' practice report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Brenden Schooler
injuryReports.returnComment: Schooler did not play in Week 10 against the Lions due to hamstring injury, and he missed the Patriots' four prior games while recovering from a back issue. His absence from Wednesday's report indicates that Schooler will be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers. He has four tackles (two solo) across five regular-season games while mostly contributing on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Schooler (hamstring) was not listed on the Patriots' injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Ben Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown did not play in the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Lions in Munich due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. With a full practice under his belt, Brown is on track to play against the Chargers on Sunday and should reclaim his starting spot at left guard while Walter Rouse reverts to a depth role on the offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Tommy DeVito
injuryReports.returnComment: With Drake Maye (fibula) hurt early in Week 10 against Detroit, DeVito stepped in at quarterback but managed to complete just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but he didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5 record, and with only rookie Behren Morton on the active roster as a healthy option to DeVito, the team may still look elsewhere if DeVito is unable to show better production.
injuryReports.injury: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that DeVito is the team's starting quarterback, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. "We're excited about that. He had a good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said of DeVito.

injuryReports.name: Alijah Vera-Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Drake Maye
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Christian Elliss
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Elliss logged 10 tackles (three solo) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Kevin Byard
injuryReports.returnComment: Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Byard registered 10 tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Lan Larison
injuryReports.returnComment: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.

injuryReports.name: Efton Chism III
injuryReports.returnComment: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Eli Raridon
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Andy Borregales
injuryReports.returnComment: Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
